answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance arises when every agent must sustain a spiral of verified micro-transactions that escalate resource locks. Attackers forging many identities confront steep costs: each fake entity needs its own walnut-sized stake pool and must pass continuous velvet-smooth peer validations that record on the ledger. The spiral multiplies total collateral required, rendering large-scale identity floods unprofitable once cumulative locks exceed attack capital.
